stories.title: Binance explains the hack: a fake job interview and an internal AI tool
stories.summary: Binance's first incident report says the $6.34B theft came from a months-long campaign that started by targeting employees, including a fake recruitment process with a malicious coding test. Withdrawals have reopened on more networks and Binance says outflows have calmed, with its next proof-of-reserves snapshot due 4 Nov.
points: In September attackers posed as executives in a fake hiring process; an employee downloaded a malicious coding test that gave access to his work computer, per The Block.
On 20 Oct they used that access and an internal AI tool to take over two other engineers' devices, then ran the wallet attack on 29 Oct, per The Block.
Binance says it has frozen or intercepted about $2.85B and replenished 98% of affected assets, per The Block.
From 1 Nov to 3 Nov, $10.97B was withdrawn and $5.695B deposited, a net outflow of about $5.28B; the next proof-of-reserves snapshot is 4 Nov, per FinanceFeeds.
At 03:00 UTC on 3 Nov hourly deposits beat withdrawals by about $10M, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: Bitcoin holds near $77,000 after more ETF outflows
stories.summary: Bitcoin dipped to about $76,300 in the European morning, per CoinDesk, and was circling $77,000 later on Tuesday, per Cointelegraph at 15:44 UTC. US spot bitcoin funds lost about $399M on Monday, led by BlackRock's IBIT.
points: Bitcoin was circling $77,000 on Tuesday, up 0.7%, per Cointelegraph (15:44 UTC).
Spot bitcoin ETFs: -$398.6M on 2 Nov; BlackRock's IBIT -$405.3M and Fidelity's FBTC +$6.7M, per NewsBTC citing Farside.
Liquidations over 24 hours were $382.6M, per CoinDesk (11:28 UTC).

stories.title: Midterms today: betting markets favour Democrats after heavy crypto spending
stories.summary: Control of Congress is decided today, and the result shapes whether the CLARITY Act, the US crypto market-structure bill, moves forward. Prediction markets moved further toward Democrats overnight. First results arrive early Wednesday Bangkok time.
points: Kalshi gave Democrats 76% and Polymarket 77% to control the Senate, up from 64.7% a week earlier on a consolidated basis; Democrats were 94% to retake the House, per Forbes.
Fairshake's own payouts reached $169.5M through 14 Oct, most of it transferred to its affiliated committees; independent spending across the network was about $136.9M, per crypto.news.
The CLARITY Act's Senate procedural vote failed 49-50 on 15 Sep and the bill has not reached the floor since, per crypto.news.
First polls close at 6:00pm ET (06:00 Wed Bangkok); the biggest wave is 8:00pm ET (08:00 Wed Bangkok) and the last, in Alaska, 1:00am ET (13:00 Wed Bangkok), per PollCheck.

briefs.title: Strategy buys 811 more bitcoin
briefs.summary: Strategy bought 811 BTC for $65.5M in the week to 1 Nov, taking its holdings to 849,327 BTC at an average cost of $75,451, per The Block.

briefs.title: Liquid's bitcoin token fully backed again
briefs.summary: Blockstream paid in the last 550 BTC, restoring full backing for Liquid's LBTC after the 6 Sep exploit of about 4,000 BTC, per The Block.

briefs.title: Old BTCPay Server hot wallets drained
briefs.summary: Bitcoin and Litecoin hot wallets on BTCPay Server 2.4.1 and earlier were drained; the fix shipped in 2.4.2, and no confirmed loss total exists yet, per The Industry Spread.

briefs.title: SEC staff add FAQs on decentralized governance
briefs.summary: SEC staff said token holders who take part in governance without ties to the team are generally not a controlling group; the FAQs are staff views with no legal force, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: Ark buys crypto stocks after the drop
briefs.summary: Ark Invest bought $3.4M of Coinbase, $2.6M of Circle and $646K of Robinhood, and sold $2.3M of Bullish, per The Block.

briefs.title: NEAR votes to cut new token issuance
briefs.summary: NEAR governance approved lowering the yearly issuance ceiling from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months, per The Block.
